title: Superlatives, so and such
titleVi: So sánh nhất, so và such
summary: Dùng the -est / the most chuẩn xác, và phân biệt so + tính từ với such + cụm danh từ.
whyItMatters: Hai lỗi này xuất hiện ở mọi bài band 6: *the most biggest problem*, *such an important issues*. Trong Task 2, *one of the most pressing issues* và *such a rapid rise* là những khung câu xuất hiện liên tục — dùng đúng thì câu tự nhiên và trang trọng, dùng sai thì giám khảo thấy ngay bạn chưa kiểm soát được cấu trúc so sánh.

sections.heading: The superlative form
body: Short adjectives take **the + -est**: *the cheapest*, *the largest*, *the biggest*. Longer adjectives take **the most**: *the most expensive*, *the most efficient*. Adjectives ending in **-y** become **-iest**: *the easiest*, *the earliest*.
The irregulars are **the best**, **the worst**, **the furthest** (or *the farthest*). Never combine the two markers: *the most biggest* is a double superlative.
Use **the least** for the bottom of a scale: *the least affordable housing in the region*. It is the natural opposite of *the most* and is far more precise than *the least cheap*.

sections.heading: in, of, and one of the
body: Use **in + place or group** when the superlative describes a whole area: *the highest life expectancy **in** Japan*, *the most competitive sector **in** the economy*.
Use **of + a specific set** when you compare named members: *the most expensive **of** the three options*, *the best **of** both worlds*.

**One of the + superlative + plural noun** is the workhorse of IELTS introductions: *one of the most pressing issues **facing** urban planners*. The noun must be **plural** — *one of the most pressing issue* is wrong because *one of* selects a member from a set.

examples.right: Hanoi is one of the fastest-growing cities in Southeast Asia.
examples.wrong: Hanoi is one of the fastest-growing city in Southeast Asia.
examples.note: **one of the …** requires a plural noun.

examples.right: It is the most expensive of the four proposals.
The country has the second highest literacy rate in the region.

sections.heading: so + adjective, such + noun phrase
body: **so** goes before an adjective or adverb with no noun: *so expensive*, *so rapidly*. **such** goes before a noun phrase, with or without an adjective: *such a rapid increase*, *such problems*.
The article sits inside the *such* phrase: **such a rapid increase**, not *a such rapid increase*. With plural or uncountable nouns there is no article: *such severe congestion*, *such high rents*.
With quantity words, use **so many / so much / so few / so little**: *so many applicants*, *so much waste*. **Such a lot of** is the informal equivalent: *such a lot of traffic*.

rows: The gap is so wide that…

sections.heading: so ... that and such ... that: result clauses
body: Both patterns introduce a **result**: *The rent was **so** high **that** few nurses could afford to live centrally.* *It was **such** a rapid change **that** regulators struggled to respond.*
Keep the *that* clause complete — a subject and a verb. Dropping *that* is common in speech but reads as careless in an essay: *The demand was so great that the scheme collapsed within a year.*

Do not confuse the result clause with **too … to**: *The rent was too high to afford* means it was impossible, not that a result followed. **So … that** reports a consequence; **too … to** reports an impossibility.

examples.right: The city grew so quickly that its transport network could not keep pace.
It was such a controversial proposal that the council postponed the vote.
Waiting lists were so long that some patients waited over a year.
examples.wrong: Waiting lists were so long that some patients waited over a year more.
examples.note: The *that* clause needs no extra quantity word.

sections.heading: Superlatives and so/such in IELTS writing
body: Superlatives are strongest when they are **qualified**. *The most expensive city in the world* is a claim you must be able to support; *one of the most expensive cities in the region* is safer and just as impressive.
In Task 1, use **the highest / the lowest / the steepest** to identify extremes, then compare: *The steepest decline occurred in manufacturing, which fell by almost a third.*
In Task 2, **such** is an elegant way to name a phenomenon without repeating it: *Cities face **such** severe congestion **that** many now ration road space.* The sentence does the work of two.

examples.right: One of the most striking features of the chart is the gap between the two groups.
examples.note: Safe, formal, and plural after *one of the*.

examples.right: The steepest fall came in 2008, when construction lost a quarter of its workforce.
Such was the demand for housing that prices doubled in five years.
examples.wrong: Such the demand for housing was that prices doubled in five years.
examples.note: Formal inversion **Such was … that**; keep the word order fixed.

commonMistakes.wrong: Air pollution is the most biggest problem in the city.
commonMistakes.right: Air pollution is the biggest problem in the city.
commonMistakes.why: Không dùng đồng thời **the most** và `-est`. Chọn một dạng so sánh nhất.

commonMistakes.wrong: Housing is one of the most pressing issue for young people.
commonMistakes.right: Housing is one of the most pressing issues for young people.
commonMistakes.why: **one of the + superlative** luôn đi với danh từ **số nhiều**, vì nó chọn một phần tử từ một tập hợp.

commonMistakes.wrong: It was a such rapid increase that regulators could not respond.
commonMistakes.right: It was such a rapid increase that regulators could not respond.
commonMistakes.why: Mạo từ **a** đứng sau *such*, không đứng trước: `such a + adj + noun`.

commonMistakes.wrong: The rent was so high prices that nurses moved away.
commonMistakes.right: The rent was so high that nurses moved away.
commonMistakes.why: **so** đứng trước tính từ, không đi với danh từ. Nếu có danh từ, dùng **such high rents that**.

commonMistakes.wrong: There were so much traffic that the road was unusable.
commonMistakes.right: There was so much traffic that the road was unusable.
commonMistakes.why: **traffic** không đếm được → *much*, và động từ số ít *was*. Lỗi này thường đi kèm với việc dùng *many* cho danh từ không đếm được.

ieltsTips: Mở bài Task 2 bằng **one of the most + adj + plural noun**: *One of the most contested questions in education policy is whether…* Cấu trúc an toàn, trang trọng, và luôn đúng số ít/số nhiều nếu bạn nhớ danh từ phải ở dạng số nhiều.

Trong Task 1, ưu tiên **the highest / the lowest / the steepest / the smallest** thay vì *very high*: *The steepest decline occurred in manufacturing.* Nêu được cực trị là một trong những tiêu chí của Task Achievement.

Dùng **such + cụm danh từ** để gọi tên một hiện tượng mà không lặp lại cả câu: ***Such** persistent inequality undermines public trust.* Gọn và học thuật hơn *This inequality is very persistent and it undermines…*
Dùng **so … that** cho quan hệ nhân quả mạnh, nhưng chỉ một lần trong bài. Nếu lặp lại, chuyển sang *as a result*, *which means that*, hoặc *consequently* để tránh đơn điệu.

exercises.question: It is ___ city in the region.
exercises.explanation: Long adjective → **the most expensive**; *in the region* follows.

exercises.question: The service is one of the ___ in the country.
It was ___ that the council postponed the vote.
exercises.explanation: **such + a + adjective + noun**; the article follows *such*.

exercises.question: There was ___ demand that the website crashed.
Which sentence is correct?
options: Hanoi is one of the fastest-growing city in Asia.
Hanoi is one of the fastest-growing cities in Asia.
Hanoi is the one of fastest-growing cities in Asia.
Hanoi is one of fastest-growing cities in Asia.

exercises.question: The ___ (high) life expectancy in the world is found in Japan.
Rents rose ___ rapidly that many families were priced out.
The city faces ___ severe congestion that journey times have doubled.
It is the second ___ (large) economy in the region.
The ___ (little) affordable housing is found in the city centre.
exercises.explanation: **the least affordable** = the bottom of the scale.
